rooted.body: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq Mosque grew from the Yemeni community that began settling in California’s San Joaquin Valley during the 1960s and 1970s. Many came to work in agriculture, while others eventually chose to remain, raise families, and make Delano their home. Over time, a close-knit Muslim community took root, held together by faith, family, and a shared responsibility to preserve their religious life for the next generation.

homes.heading: From Homes to a Masjid
homes.body: Before there was a permanent mosque, local Muslims gathered for prayer in family homes, including the home of Mohammed and Irma Abdullah, who were among those instrumental in establishing a lasting place of worship for the community. From these early gatherings came the effort to create a permanent masjid, and around 2000, Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq Mosque was established in Delano.

namesake.heading: Why Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq?
namesake.body: The mosque was named in honor of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), the close companion of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the first caliph of the Muslim community. Known by the title al-Siddiq, “the Truthful,” he is remembered for his faith, loyalty, generosity, and steadfast support of Islam.

worship.heading: A Place to Worship and Learn
worship.body: From its beginnings, the mosque has been more than a place for the daily prayers and Jumu’ah. It has also served as a madrasa and center for Islamic learning, where children and adults study their faith, learn the Qur’an, and gather as a community. Today, Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq Mosque continues to serve Delano’s Muslims while carrying forward the faith and community that first took root here generations ago.
